title: Apollo 11: Catching Some Sun
explanation:
# Moon Landing Science in Action

On July 20, 1969, astronaut Buzz Aldrin unfurled a sheet of aluminum foil on the Moon's surface—not for leftovers, but to catch invisible particles streaming from the Sun like cosmic rain, a bold experiment captured in this iconic photograph by Neil Armstrong. This ingenious solar wind collector, along with 22 kilograms of moon rocks brought back to Earth, gave scientists their first direct samples of material from the Sun itself and secrets about how our star constantly bombards the solar system.
